regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks unambiguous until you note that GVA likely trails by 150–200 bps and core sector growth decelerated to 4.8% YoY even as IIP capital goods accelerated to 16.9% YoY — the investment side is pulling ahead while the output side drags. PMI composite at 55.9 is services-led (55.2) with manufacturing (55.1) only recently recovering from 52.8; the breadth is narrower than the headline suggests. The inversion: if capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity triggers private capex, the next question is whether deposit-constrained banks can fund it.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 5.54% YoY is 44 bps above RBI's upper tolerance band, but the composition is what matters: food at 7.74% YoY and fuel at 22.93% YoY are doing the work, while core CPI sits at 3.9% YoY — the 28th percentile historically. The gap between headline and core is 164 bps and widening, which ordinarily would give the RBI room to look through the spike. But WPI at 9.92% YoY tells a different story: producer prices are running hot, and with a 2–3 quarter lag, core CPI will feel it. The RBI's own forecast of 5.1% YoY is already above target — any further crude pass-through closes the cut window entirely.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth of 17.8% YoY is a 160 bps divergence that has widened for two consecutive months — the CD ratio at 81% sits at the 73rd percentile historically. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was the pre-taper period of FY13–14; within four quarters, the RBI was forced into emergency tightening. Services credit at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile) and vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY (68th percentile) are the acceleration engines — both rising for two straight months. The second-order risk: if deposit mobilisation doesn't catch up, the RBI reaches for macro-prudential tools — risk-weight hikes on unsecured lending — before it reaches for the repo rate.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate calculus is shifting: with CPI at 5.54% YoY, the real repo rate is effectively negative 29 bps — accommodative by accident, not design. The RBI's inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY already embeds a cut-deferral signal, yet the market is still pricing some easing probability. The inversion: if Brent holds above $100/bbl and the INR stays near 95, imported inflation feeds back into CPI with a two-quarter lag — the RBI doesn't cut, and the long end of the curve reprices upward, compressing housing affordability and corporate capex IRRs simultaneously.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (up from 16.1% YoY) and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%) are the two numbers that matter: utilisation crossing 77% has historically been the threshold at which private capex intentions convert to orders. The bull case is self-reinforcing — services credit at 24.3% YoY and vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY suggest the demand signal is real. The bear case: core sector at 4.8% YoY decelerated from 5.0% YoY, and core sector is the physical infrastructure that capital goods orders eventually become. If steel and cement dispatch don't confirm, the IIP capital goods print is orders, not installations.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is at the 73rd percentile, but the composition matters: passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are falling for two consecutive months (from 26.1% YoY), while two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY rebounded sharply. This is the classic India dual-economy signal — mass-market rural consumption (two-wheelers) recovering while urban discretionary (passenger vehicles) fades. E-commerce GMV growth at 12.4% YoY sits at the 15th percentile, corroborating the urban demand softness. The GST number flatters: at ₹2.03 lakh crore, it looks like a demand story, but with fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY taxing disposable income, the volume signal is weaker than the value signal.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1%→19.4% credit; 9.9%→17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 57th percentile. Services credit surging at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile), rising 2 straight months.","implication":"The deposit acceleration masks a structural problem: banks are chasing credit growth faster than retail deposits can sustain. NBFC funding stress is real — wholesale borrowing costs will rise. Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% (they'll poach deposits). Underweight NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities. RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 to ease deposit pressure, not growth concerns. Position for a 25-50 bps cut by June.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile is elevated but not crisis-level. The last time it breached 82% (2022), RBI tightened aggressively. This time, growth is strong enough that RBI will ease instead.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Beyond Capital Goods","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest, 52nd percentile), up from 16.1% YoY. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (48th percentile), up from 75.6% — now in the zone where capex accelerates. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (50th percentile), a slight deceleration from 5%, but services credit (24.3% YoY, 79th percentile) and vehicle credit (19.7% YoY, 68th percentile) both rising sharply. PMI manufacturing at 55.1 index (75th percentile), services at 55.2 index (84th percentile).","implication":"Capex is broadening from traditional capital goods into services and consumer durables. This is late-cycle but healthy — not a bubble. Overweight: capital goods manufacturers, cement, steel, and commercial vehicle OEMs. Avoid: housing finance (credit growth at 11.1% YoY, falling 2 months) and consumer discretionary tied to credit-dependent segments. The capex cycle will sustain 6-8% GDP growth through FY27.","pct_10y":52,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-cycle; historically, capex accelerates when CU crosses 78-80%. We're at the inflection point. This level preceded 3-4 quarters of strong capex in 2015-16 and 2021-22.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 93rd Percentile, But Ticket Size Inflates","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (latest, 93rd percentile), rising 3 consecutive months (₹29,845→₹31,961→₹32,297→₹32,490 cr / month). SIP accounts at 10.0646 mn (2nd percentile, historically low), but SIP AUM at ₹17.86 lakh cr (89th percentile). Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (80th percentile), up from ₹29,329 cr / month. DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile). But NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile, down from ₹3,051 cr / month).","implication":"SIP inflows are strong, but the story is NOT mass retail — it's affluent money. Average SIP ticket size is rising (AUM +40% YoY vs accounts +10% YoY). This is late-cycle behaviour: high-net-worth individuals locking in systematic buys before a potential correction. Retail is not chasing new schemes (NFO collections at 2nd percentile). Position: reduce equity exposure; rotate into quality large-caps with pricing power. SIP growth will decelerate when markets correct 8-12%.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile are near all-time highs, but SIP accounts at 2nd percentile is a red flag. The last time this divergence occurred (2021), markets peaked within 6 months. Affluent money is front-running retail.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile, CAD Widening","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, 95th percentile), up from 20.05% YoY — rising 2 consecutive months. Brent crude at $110.75/bbl (down from $116.72/bbl but still elevated, 77th percentile). WTI at $102.25/bbl (84th percentile). FAO food index at 136 index (61st percentile), up from 134.5 index. India's headline CPI at 5.54% YoY (52nd percentile), up from 4.83% YoY, driven by food (7.74% YoY, 57th percentile) and fuel. WPI at 9.92% YoY (67th percentile), up from 9.78% YoY.","implication":"Fuel inflation is the primary driver of headline CPI overshoot. RBI's 5.1% inflation forecast (53rd percentile) will be breached if oil stays >$110/bbl. Current account deficit will widen if crude averages $105-115/bbl for the next 2 quarters. Hedge: long INR (it will weaken further as oil imports rise), short refiners with weak hedges, long fertiliser stocks (they'll benefit from subsidy support). Avoid: consumer staples with low pricing power. RBI will stay on pause, not cut, until fuel inflation moderates.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is the highest in 3 years. The last time it was this elevated (2022), RBI hiked rates 190 bps. This time, growth is too weak for aggressive tightening, but rate cuts are off the table.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"BOJ Tightening Breaks Carry Trade Funding","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, highest in 40 years), up from 1% p.a. — rising 2 consecutive months (0.75%→1%→1.25%). Fed funds at 3.75% p.a. (68th percentile), up from 3.63% p.a., rising 2 in a row. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (63rd percentile), up from 2.25% p.a., rising 2 in a row. US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% yield (90th percentile), down from 5.13% yield but still elevated. US PMI composite at 58.4 index (91st percentile), rising 2 months. Global PMI at 54.3 index (84th percentile).","implication":"BOJ's rate hike to 1.25% is a structural break for carry trades funded in yen. Yen will strengthen, forcing unwinding of long positions in high-beta assets (India, EM equities, commodities). INR will face headwinds from both carry trade unwind and oil imports. FII equity flows will turn negative (already at -₹49,935 cr / month, 17th percentile). Position: reduce India equity exposure by 10-15%; hedge INR at 96-97 levels; overweight USD cash. The next 4-6 weeks will see EM volatility spike as carry trades unwind.","pct_10y":100,"pct_note":"BOJ at 1.25% is the highest rate in 40 years, marking the end of the yen carry era. The last major carry unwind (2015) saw EM equities fall 15-20% in 2 months. India is vulnerable given FII outflows already underway.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakens to 95.24, Reserves Pressure Mounting","data_text":"INR/USD at 95.24 ₹ (latest, 89th percentile), up from 94.93 ₹ — weakening 2 of last 5 observations (96.15→97.09→96.15→95.24→94.34→95.24). Signal tagged strong-negative (score: -78). FII equity net at -₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile), a sharp reversal from positive flows. DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) is offsetting FII outflows, but this is unsustainable. Brent at $110.75/bbl (77th percentile) is widening the current account deficit. US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% yield (90th percentile) is attracting capital away from India.","implication":"INR is under structural pressure from three vectors: (1) FII outflows due to BOJ carry unwind, (2) rising oil import bill (fuel inflation at 95th percentile), (3) US Treasury yields at 90th percentile attracting capital. RBI will defend 96-97 levels but cannot hold indefinitely without rate hikes. Expect INR to trade 95.5-97 over the next 2 quarters. Overweight: exporters with USD revenues (IT, pharma, auto components). Underweight: importers and consumer discretionary. Hedge: long USD forwards at 96-97 levels.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile weakness is the highest in 2 years. The last time INR was this weak (2022), RBI hiked rates 190 bps and FII flows reversed. This time, RBI is unlikely to hike, so INR weakness will persist.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Decoupling From IT Stock Proxy","data_text":"Office absorption at 2.6 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, data sparse but recent: 14.1→4→5.3→18.7→5.3→24.6 mn sq ft / quarter, highly volatile). Office vacancy at 14.7% vacant (43rd percentile), up from 14.5% vacant. Nifty IT index embedded in Nifty50 at 22,600 index (73rd percentile), down from 22,687 index. But Nifty50 PMI services at 55.2 index (84th percentile), and services credit at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile). Rent in Bengaluru at ₹103.6/sqft/mo (59th percentile), up from ₹102.8/sqft/mo. Rent in Mumbai at ₹156/sqft/mo (59th percentile), up from ₹144.4/sqft/mo.","implication":"Office absorption is NOT driven by traditional IT services anymore — it's Global Capability Centers (GCCs) and non-IT services (fintech, consulting, BPO). Nifty IT is a poor proxy for commercial real estate demand. The buyer is multinational capex, not Indian IT services. This means: (1) Commercial RE REITs (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield) are undervalued — they're capturing GCC capex, not IT headcount cycles. (2) Traditional IT services stocks are overvalued — they're shedding office space, not expanding. (3) Rent inflation in Tier-1 cities (Bengaluru +0.8/sqft, Mumbai +11.6/sqft) is structural, not cyclical. Position: Overweight commercial REITs; underweight Nifty IT; long office landlords in Bengaluru and Mumbai. This decoupling will persist for 2-3 years as GCC capex cycles diverge from IT services cycles.","pct_10y":59,"pct_note":"Office rents at 59th percentile are mid-cycle, but the composition of demand has shifted. The last time office absorption decoupled from IT stocks (2019-20), commercial REITs outperformed IT by 300+ bps over 18 months. GCC capex is the new structural driver.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP Headline, 4.8% Core Sector — Investment Leads, Output Lags

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY (64th percentile), with IIP capital goods accelerating to 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity — the investment cycle is broadening.
  • But core sector growth decelerated to 4.8% YoY from 5.0% YoY — steel, cement, and electricity output are not confirming the capital goods order book.
  • PMI composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) is services-led; manufacturing recovered to 55.1 from 52.8 but remains below its six-month average.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural recovery; passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY falling for two consecutive months signal urban softness.

The tension: The investment cycle and the PMI headline both point up, but the physical output indicators — core sector, PV sales, e-commerce GMV at the 15th percentile — point sideways. Orders are not yet installations.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY: a second consecutive print below 5.0% YoY would signal the capex upcycle is front-loaded in orders, not yet in output.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Re-Acceleration Meets EM Tightening — BOJ at 40-Year High Breaks the Carry

The facts:

  • US PMI composite at 58.4 (91st percentile), rising for two consecutive months — DM demand is re-accelerating, not slowing.
  • But BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, highest in 40 years), rising for two consecutive months — yen carry unwind is structural, not episodic.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 4.96% yield (90th percentile) — real tightening is embedded in the long end even as the Fed holds at 3.75% p.a.
  • Global PMI composite at 54.3 (84th percentile) with China PMI recovering to 52.1 — but China GDP at 4.4% YoY (46th percentile) limits commodity reflation.

The tension: DM surveys signal growth re-acceleration, but the BOJ's 40-year rate high is unwinding the carry trade that funded EM equity inflows — including India's. The two cannot coexist for long.

Bottom line: BOJ's next move is the single most important global variable for India liquidity; a third consecutive hike above 1.25% p.a. would accelerate FII outflows beyond the DII absorption capacity.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds the Market — But DII Absorption Has a Ceiling

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising for three consecutive months — retail flows are structurally anchored.
  • DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) is absorbing FII equity outflows of -₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile) almost exactly.
  • But NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile) from ₹3,051 cr / month — institutional conviction is not following retail inertia.
  • MF AUM fell to ₹82.64 lakh cr from ₹87.08 lakh cr despite rising SIP inflows — mark-to-market erosion is outpacing fresh flows.

The tension: SIP inflows create the appearance of liquidity resilience, but MF AUM is falling and NFO collections are at a decade low — the market is being held by autopilot retail, not by fresh institutional conviction.

Bottom line: If FII outflows sustain above -₹50,000 cr / month for a second consecutive month, DII absorption will require redemption pressure to ease — watch weekly MF equity redemption data.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand Holds Premium Segment; Equities Price Growth the Bond Market Doubts

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (up 8 pp), with 25% share within premium/luxury; remittances at $144.8 bn (16.2% YoY) provide the funding floor.
  • Premium and luxury supply (₹80 lakh–₹2.5 cr bands) accounts for 58% of launches; Hyderabad leads with sales up 15% YoY and launches up 120% YoY — but 28 months of unsold inventory is a supply overhang.
  • Nifty 50 at 22,600 (73rd percentile), falling for five of the last six sessions — India VIX rising to 16.86 (12th percentile but up four of last five days) signals building unease.
  • But REIT units are pricing distress: Embassy at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down 12–29% from prior levels despite office leasing in Bengaluru at 5.2 mn sq ft / quarter.

The tension: NRI demand and GCC-driven office leasing support real asset fundamentals, but listed proxies — REITs and Nifty IT — are being sold. The physical market and the financial market are pricing different realities.

Bottom line: Overweight physical premium residential in Bengaluru and Hyderabad where NRI demand and GCC absorption are structural; avoid REIT units until the FII outflow cycle stabilises.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — Crude Holds the Key

The facts:

  • Crude pass-through to CAD: Brent at $110.75/bbl (77th percentile) — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's annual import bill; INR at 95.24 (89th percentile) amplifies the pass-through into domestic fuel inflation already at 22.93% YoY.
  • BOJ carry unwind accelerating: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) with FII equity outflows at -₹49,935 cr / month — a third BOJ hike would break the DII absorption equilibrium.
  • Credit-deposit divergence triggering macro-prudential action: CD ratio at 81% (73rd percentile) with credit at 19.4% YoY vs deposits at 17.8% YoY — RBI risk-weight action on unsecured lending is the most likely near-term policy move.
  • US CPI re-acceleration delaying Fed cuts: US CPI at 3.72% YoY rising for three consecutive months — if the Fed holds or hikes, the US 10Y stays above 4.9% yield and India's rate-cut window closes entirely.

The tension: All four risks share a common amplifier: a crude price that refuses to fall below $100/bbl keeps CAD wide, INR weak, and domestic inflation above the RBI's tolerance — which in turn keeps the policy rate on hold and the carry trade unattractive.

Bottom line: Watch Brent this week: a sustained break above $115/bbl would simultaneously widen CAD by 60+ bps, push CPI above 6.0% YoY, and force the RBI to defend the INR — the trifecta that ends the growth narrative.

"}
